accepted.label: a
accepted.text: Some candidates may use the Cartesian form in (a) possibly having done (b) first. E.g. $y=\frac{4x+11}{x+5}\Rightarrow\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{4(x+5)-4x-11}{(x+5)^2}\left(=\frac{9}{(x+5)^2}\right)$ $t=3\Rightarrow x=\frac{9}{2}-5=-\frac{1}{2}$ $\Rightarrow\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{9}{\left(-\frac{1}{2}+5\right)^2}=\frac{4}{9}$. This would require a complete method to find the Cartesian equation and then B1 for the correct derivative. Then M1 for a complete method attempting the derivative and substituting for x or t and A1 for 4/9 as in the main scheme. The marks for obtaining the Cartesian equation can score in (b) provided their Cartesian equation is seen or used in (b). (i.e. if they do (a) first)
